question.problem:
Suppose we take a random sample of size $n=75$ from a population where $45%$ of the population has a particular characteristic. Find a normal approximation for the probability that less than $50%$ of the sample has the characteristic. You may assume that the population size is significantly larger than the sample size.

*Hint: $Φ(z)$ is the cumulative distribution function for the standard normal distribution.*
question.worked_solution:
Given a population in which a proportion $p$ of the population has a particular characteristic, the sampling distribution of the sample proportion $\overset{^}{\,p}$ can be approximated as

$$
\overset{^}{\,p}∼N(p,\frac{p(1-p)}{n}),
$$

where the sample size $n$ is much smaller than the population size, $np>5,$ and $n(1-p)>5.$

In our case

- the sample size is $n=75,$ and

- the population proportion is $p=0.45.$

Now, since

$$
np=75(0.45)=33.75>5
$$

and

$$
n(1-p)=75(1-0.45)=41.25>5,
$$

and $n=75$ is much smaller than the population size, we can apply the above approximation.

The sampling distribution of the sample proportion, in this case, can be approximated as

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{^}{\,p} & ∼N(p,\frac{p(1-p)}{n}) \\  & ∼N(0.45,\frac{0.45(1-0.45)}{75}) \\  & ∼N(0.45,0.0033).\end{aligned}
$$

The probability we wish to find is
$P(\overset{^}{\,p}<0.5).$
So, we convert $\overset{^}{\,p}$ to a standard normal random variable by $z$-scoring:

$$
\begin{aligned}P(\overset{^}{\,p}\le 0.5) & =P(Z\le \frac{0.5-0.45}{\sqrt{0.0033}}) \\  & ≈P(Z\le 0.87) \\  & =Φ(0.87)\end{aligned}
$$
